newsitem.title: UK: UK housing starts fall four pct in 3 mths to April.
newsitem.headline: UK housing starts fall four pct in 3 mths to April.

text.p: Total British housing starts fell a seasonally adjusted four percent in the three months to April copmared with the previous three while total completions were down two percent, the Department of Environment said on Monday.
In the latest three months, 50,400 dwellings were started, up 16 percent on the same three months a year ago, while completions at 42,800 were up 1 percent.
The DoE provisionally estimated that 18,000 dwellings were started in April compared with 15,100 in April 1996. Completions numbered 15,200 compared with 14,500 in April last year.
Private enterprise starts were down 4 percent in the three months to April while completions were up by 3 per cent.
Housing Association starts of new dwellings in the three months February to April were down compared with the previous three months. Completions also fell back.
Both starts and completions by local authorities and government departments remained at a low level.
